definition: Obscurity means the state of attracting no notice — unknown or forgotten by the wider world.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word obscurity. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know obscurity should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The chess variant spent decades in obscurity before a streaming series made it a lunchtime craze.
Anonymity hides only the name - a donor can stay unnamed while the gift makes headlines; obscurity goes further, leaving the person and the work unknown alike.
Oblivion outdoes obscurity: an obscure poet still sits findable on a library shelf, while a poet in oblivion has vanished from every shelf and every memory.

Namelessness is the plain condition of having no name attached — an unsigned painting, an unmarked grave. Obscurity is wider: an obscure person's name may be perfectly findable, yet nobody looks, because the person and the work alike sit outside the world's notice.

Insignificance means mattering too little to affect anything — small stakes, no consequences either way. Obscurity measures notice, not weight: a discovery can be hugely important and still sit in obscurity for decades, unknown to the wider world until someone finally stumbles onto it.

Obscurity is built on Latin obscurus, 'covered over, darkened.' The old covering-root behind -scur- made no other common English word: its only living relatives are obscure and obscurity themselves, so this family tree stops after one branch.
Obscurity means the state of attracting no notice — unknown or forgotten by the wider world.
Most words live and die in obscurity.
'Snollygoster' had its brief career in 1890s newsprint, then sank: no textbook carried it, no speech revived it, and only dictionary editors, turning the yellowed pages, ever met it again.
Obscurity is exact for that sunk-from-view state: the word still exists - a determined reader can find it - but nobody knows it, uses it, or misses it.
Not anonymity (a name kept off known work) and not yet oblivion (erased even from the dictionary): obscurity is the wide, quiet shelf between.
Obscurity names the state of being unknown or forgotten - careers begin in it and often end in it.
Anonymity hides only the name; a person in obscurity is unknown, work and all.
And keep the mirror straight: obscurity means the world overlooks you; oblivious (this unit) means you overlook the world.

In 1957, a Kansas high-school teacher named Ruth Alcott self-published forty copies of a booklet on prime numbers.
It then spent half a century in near-total obscurity: her name was right there on the cover, the booklet sat cataloged in three libraries, and in fifty years the checkout card gathered four stamps.
Nothing was hidden and nothing was secret; the world simply never glanced her way.
When a graduate student finally cited the booklet in 2009, number theorists were startled to find a key result worked out decades early.
Alcott had not been ignored because she was wrong, or concealed, or unimportant -- only unlooked-at.
